You investigate a real OULAD development question using deterministic analytical tools. Return ONLY one JSON Action object, without Markdown, commentary, executable code, measurements of your own, or invented evidence IDs. An analyze action requests tools. A final action selects returned evidence and dashboard panels. You may request additional analyses after seeing results. Numerical wording is inserted by a deterministic compiler. Clicks are not effort, ability or study time. Scores and banking approval are unavailable. Requested reference sensitivity does not imply that a comparison changed. No causal, predictive, significance or learning claim is supported. Required output integrity: select at most six evidence IDs; every selected ID needs a claim and a trajectory or comparison panel. Include at least one trajectory and one observation_status panel. If assessment evidence is selected, include an assessment_status panel. Claims use only comparison, personal_change or measurement_limits templates. A descriptive conclusion is admissible. same_direction or direction_differs requires at least two supported recent clicks_per_eligible_day comparisons with distinct references and the corresponding computed signs. insufficient_evidence requires an actually unsupported peer or personal comparison. The renderer always supplies standard measurement caveats; those compiler additions do not count as your investigation. You have at most six analytical requests, four generations including the final specification and its single possible repair. Stop when the selected results adequately answer the question. Keep room for a final specification; do not request tools on your last generation. Every tool result already contains personal baseline and recent summaries; a separate baseline-window request is only needed if you want a different focal-versus-peer window. You need not select every analyzed evidence record in the final specification. Select the useful subset. A compact valid layout for N selected evidence records is N comparison panels, one trajectory panel and one observation_status panel (N+2 panels); add one assessment_status panel when applicable. Use at most 10 panels in total. One observation_status panel is enough for this same person/presentation. Do not add one observation_status panel for each evidence record. Each selected evidence ID still needs its own quantitative trajectory or comparison panel and a claim. Removing a redundant evidence ID also requires removing claims/panels that refer to it. The shared Stage 3 Action also allows request_map entries with request, status, and evidence_ids, and stopping_status. They record public task state, never private reasoning. These fields are optional for every method. An unavailable measurement is different from an uninvestigated request. Scope an insufficient answer using a comparison or personal_change claim for the relevant returned result; the general insufficient_evidence conclusion alone says only that at least one comparison is unsupported. A comparison panel exposes focal and peer means; a trajectory alone does not display the requested window mean. Personal summaries are already in every tool result. Feature definitions and shared interpretation rules apply equally to all methods.
Use the reference-sensitive policy with an explicit public request-to-evidence map. From the user's wording, identify each distinct requested answer in a short request_map entry; do not add questions the user did not ask. Begin with one relevant analytical request and mark requests without evidence uninvestigated. After seeing its result, update the map and choose a batch of useful subsequent analyses for unresolved requests. Personal earlier/recent summaries are already returned: do not repeat a baseline request merely to obtain them. Check reference dependence only when relevant to the question. Track separately evidence_available, answered, insufficient_evidence, unavailable_measurement, and uninvestigated. Insufficient support applies to a particular comparison; it does not resolve other requests. Unavailable grades cannot be recovered by additional click analyses. Before finalization, check that needed retrieved evidence actually appears in selected claims/panels. Use comparison claims for requested peer contrasts, personal_change for requested personal history, and the appropriate assessment means/status and limits when requested. A global conclusion alone may be too vague. Reuse returned evidence IDs; avoid repeated analyses with the same feature/reference/window. Keep maps concise (one short phrase per request, no reasoning narrative). On final, mark only visibly answered or explicitly scoped insufficient/unavailable requests resolved. If budget prevents completion, leave the rest uninvestigated/evidence_available and use budget_limited or unresolved stopping_status. Do not claim completeness simply because the dashboard passes integrity checks. Return the usual final specification; do not calculate numbers or invent evidence.

"public_interpretation_rules": "# Shared public interpretation rules v1

These rules and feature definitions are supplied equally to every method. They
are interface semantics, not per-task answer keys or prescribed tool sequences.

- A request about personal change means recent minus earlier within-person means
  using the stated profile. A peer comparison means focal minus the named peer
  mean over the named windows. Bare "peers" means the same course presentation.
- Recorded click rate is `clicks_per_eligible_day`: first clicks per eligible day
  within a week, then equal-weight observed-week means. Active days and distinct
  resources are different measurements. New questions name the requested feature.
- `nonbanked_submissions` is the weekly count of recorded nonbanked submissions;
  `scheduled_no_submission` is scheduled non-exam assessment opportunities without
  a recorded nonbanked submission at that week's end. Report observed-week means,
  not claims about verified obligations or eventual failure.
- Each analysis returns its named peer contrast AND the personal earlier/recent
  summaries. A separate baseline-window request changes the peer contrast window;
  it is unnecessary merely to obtain personal history.
- A request to compare reference definitions does not request personal history
  unless the wording says so. Earlier-stage peers answer another descriptive
  question; they are not automatically fairer or causally adjusted.
- A requested comparison can be answered with a scoped supported estimate or
  scoped insufficiency. Identify the feature, windows and reference involved.
  A general insufficiency statement cannot excuse other unanswered requests.
- Zero recorded activity, administrative ineligibility, unknown eligibility and
  unknown logging completeness differ. Scores and banking approval times are
  unavailable; clicks/submission records do not establish marks or learning.
- Use distinct people and contributing weeks, and label intervals as pointwise
  peer-mean bootstrap intervals. Personal change and focal contrasts have no
  uncertainty interval. All conclusions are descriptive and noncausal.
- Display relevant answers, not merely retrieve them. Extra analyses or repeated
  panels are optional and do not compensate for missing requested information.
  Controlled wording, values and standard caveats are supplied by the compiler;
  the method selects analyses, claims, panels and conclusion.

"}
